question.text: Nelson previously beat French forces and sank the Orient at a battle in this river's delta, from which Cleopatra's ships departed to fight at Actium.
question.clue: The Bari and related peoples migrated up this river after the end of the baqt ("bukt") treaty, which caused kingdoms led from Soba and Dongola to decline and allowed the Funj Sultanate to expand along this river.

swap.text: Ramses the Great was a pharaoh of the 19th Dynasty of Egypt, during this period of Egyptian history, which saw such rulers as Thutmose III and Akhenaten. It is contrasted with the Old and Middle Kingdoms.
swap.clue: Nobility from Byblos and other Levantine cities were forced to be educated in Kemet during this period, one of its many characteristic imperial policies.

question.text: The only remaining wonder of the ancient world is this structure, which was built for Pharaoh Khufu [koo-foo] at Giza.
question.answerHtml: The Great Pyramid of Giza (accept The Great Pyramid of Khufu or reasonable equivalents)
question.clue: Slave labor was long thought to have been used to build this structure, but many archaeologists believe that thousands of skilled laborers were used instead over a 20 year period.

swap.leadin: The Greeks referred to this man as Ozymandias.
swap.text: Name this "great" Egyptian pharaoh who defeated the Nile "Sea People" and claimed a victory at the 1274 BCE Battle of Kadesh.
swap.clue: This builder of a "Sistine Chapel of Ancient Egypt" brokered a treaty with Hattusili III, and built a temple at Abu Simbel for his wife Nefertari.

question.leadin: This battle was fought along the Orontes River.
question.text: Name this battle fought between forces divided into divisions such as Ra and Amun against Hittite forces under Muwatalli II.
question.clue: One side of this battle was split into divisions such as the Ptah and Amun, and it was fought along the Orontes River.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about explorers who weren't from Europe.
swap.text: The ancient Egyptian explorer Neshi was commissioned by this female pharaoh to lead her expedition to Punt. This woman ruled as regent for her son Thutmose III, which stirred his resentment to the point where he tried to erase her from the historical record.
swap.clue: This ruler's mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari includes a relief detailing a trading expedition to the Land of Punt, which brought back incense and myrrh trees.

question.leadin: This city's "Supremacy" over Greece lasted for much of the early 4th century BC.
question.text: Name this central Greek city whose elite troops, the Sacred Band, consisted of 150 pairs of male lovers. It was legendarily the home of King Oedipus and was founded by Cadmus.
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.leadin: One ruler of this name beheaded Pompey, and another erected the Rosetta Stone.
swap.text: Give this regnal name of rulers whose queens were often named Arsinoe or Berenice.
swap.clue: One ruler of this name won the Battle of Raphia against Antiochus the Great and married his sister, Arsinoe III.

question.leadin: This artifact shows two lions with serpentine necks intertwining as well as rows of figures with their heads between their legs.
question.text: Name this object likely used for applying makeup. It depicts its subject with two crowns, each representing a different kingdom.
question.clue: This object's main companion piece may feature a predecessor of the Nine Bows insignia, and depicts a marriage ceremony with Neithhotep.

swap.leadin: While working in this city, Eratosthenes ("eh-ra-TOSS-thuh-neez") of Cyrene produced the first known estimate of the circumference of the Earth.
swap.text: Name this ancient center of learning that flourished as the capital of Ptolemaic ("toll-uh-MAY-ic") Egypt. This city's namesake Great Library and its large collection of papyrus scrolls were burned down by Julius Caesar in 48 BC.
swap.clue: After the Battle of Actium, Mark Antony and Cleopatra committed suicide in this city, where Euclid and Eratosthenes performed research during the Hellenistic Period.

question.leadin: Name some things about the Diadochi.
question.text: Through the Partition of Babylon, this successor of Alexander was appointed satrap of Egypt. This ruler's namesake dynasty would rule until Cleopatra's suicide and the Roman annexation of Egypt.
question.clue: He acquired his first wife Artacama during the mass wedding at Susa, cemented a later alliance by marrying Antipater's daughter Eurydice, and finally chose another wife, Berenice, to elevate to the title of queen.

swap.leadin: It succeeded Alexander the Great's rule in Egypt and was named for the Macedonian general who founded it.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that ruled from 323 BCE to 30 BCE.
swap.clue: It supplied several of the ships destroyed by Agrippa at Actium, and it was an ally of Mark Antony.

question.leadin: Josephus claimed that these people founded Jerusalem and gave a false etymology for their name deriving from the Greek for "Shepherd-kings."
question.text: Name these people whose name comes from the ancient Egyptian for "rulers of foreign lands." These people's 15th Dynasty ruled from Avaris during the Second Intermediate Period.
question.clue: In a satirical story, a ruler of these people complains that he can't sleep because of noisy hippos in a letter addressed to Seqenenre ("sek-en-EN-ray") Tao.

swap.text: This adjective names the form of common Greek speech that became the country's standard language via reforms passed in 1982. This adjective also refers to a form of ancient Egyptian writing used by common people, as opposed to priests or royal scribes.
swap.clue: This Egyptian script derived from hieratic ("high-RAT-ick"), whose common name means "popular." The Rosetta Stone uses Greek, Egyptian hieroglyphics, and this cursive script.

question.text: Menander's plays are among the roughly half a million papyri unearthed at this Egyptian site, which is named for a "sharp-nosed fish."
question.clue: Many of the finds from the excavation at this site led by Grenfell and Hunt are housed in the Sackler Library in Oxford.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about dubious claims of modern technology existing in the ancient Near East.
swap.text: Ramses II ordered the alteration of hieroglyphs from Seti I's (the first's) temple at Abydos (aa-bee-DAHS), producing an image that 1990s Internet theorists noted as resembling this kind of vehicle.
swap.clue: The company Sikorsky won a bid to produce these vehicles, which are called Marine One when they transport the US President.

question.leadin: Answer the following about water in ancient Egypt.
question.text: Two massive statues known by this name were built by Amenhotep III to stand guard over his mortuary temples at the Theban metropolis across the Nile from Luxor. Several projects have been designed around preventing the Nile from eating away at these statues.
question.clue: These are two giant statues of the deified Amenhotep III, one of which depicts his wife Tiy and mother Mutememwia. They flank the entrance of his mortuary temple pylon across the Nile from Luxor.

swap.leadin: Seti I fought a war against these people, whom he called the "Tjehnu," and the Great Karnak Inscription describes the defeat of their "Great Chief" Meryey's alliance with the Lukka and four Sea Peoples.
swap.text: Name this people, who at one point ruled Egypt in a dynasty descended from Osorkon the Elder. A stele recounting one pharaoh's victory over these people is also one of the first documents to mention the word "Israel."

question.leadin: It formally began when Menuhotep I ousted the rulers of the House of Khety. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this period that began with the reuniting of Egypt and was undone by a schism between Theban rulers and foreign usurpers who seized Memphis and established a dynasty based in Avaris.
question.clue: The fnal rulers of this period were called the Xois Dynasty since they moved the capital there.

swap.text: This man became the third head librarian of the Library around 240 BCE, and he may be best known for developing a namesake "sieve" that identifies prime numbers.
swap.clue: To accomplish one of his tasks, this man hired a number of bematists to walk 5,000 stadia.
